run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T13:40:21Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend is explained by frontend's AdService dependency: Deployment ad in namespace otel-demo was rolled out at 13:39:10Z, its only old pod (ad-554b849958-gcmfq) was scaled down and deleted at 13:39:13Z, and the replacement pod (ad-d89765fb5-whfnz) was reported Ready at 13:39:13Z even though the AdService application had not started yet (its only log line, 'Ad service starting.', is timestamped 13:43:23Z). Neither the old nor the new ReplicaSet template defines a readinessProbe, so Kubernetes considered the new pod available as soon as its container started (13:39:12Z), and the Service endpoint (100.96.1.122) pointed at a process that was not serving. Ad's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds server-span rate fell from 1.22/s at 13:38 to 0 from 13:42 through 13:49 and resumed at 13:50. In exactly that interval frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR (0.36/s at 13:40 rising to 1.29/s at 13:42, ~1.18-1.24/s through 13:47), together with error spans on GET, GET /api/data and 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' at the same rates, and small tcp.connect error spans; frontend's total error-span rate rose from 0 before 13:40 to a peak of ~4.19/s at 13:46-13:47 and returned to 0 by 13:52, matching the alert start 13:40:21Z. frontend-proxy shows the same error pattern on its ingress and frontend-egress spans, consistent with propagating frontend 5xx. The ad pod itself is Running, Ready and has 0 restarts, and no other service shows error spans on this path; ad emitted no ERROR-status spans, so its gap was a serving gap, not an application error burst. The rollout was performed by ad's own controller (SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete/ScalingReplicaSet), i.e. a rollout, not damage; what triggered it and why the AdService process took minutes to start are not established by the available evidence (change_history is not integrated).

claims.text: At 13:45Z frontend carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans at 1.037/s on span_name GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, plus tcp.connect error spans at 0.0222/s; all other frontend operations (cart, checkout, product-catalog, recommendation routes) had 0 error rate, so the failing path is the AdService call behind /api/data.

frontend's error-span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) was 0 from 12:45 through 13:39, became 0.5/s at 13:40, rose to 4.17-4.19/s at 13:46-13:47, declined to 2.36/s at 13:49, 1.62/s at 13:50, 0.70/s at 13:51 and returned to 0 from 13:52 onward, while its non-error span rate stayed roughly 40-55/s throughout.

The frontend error is ads-specific: per-operation error rate for frontend is identical (0.356/s at 13:40, 1.0/s at 13:41, 1.29/s at 13:42, 1.18-1.24/s at 13:46-13:47, 0.52/s at 13:48, 0 at 13:49 onward) for GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, while grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout stayed at 0 error rate; a small tcp.connect error rate (0.078/s at 13:40 down to 0.022/s at 13:45-13:47) accompanied the outage.

ad stopped serving GetAds during the same interval: its oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span rate fell from 1.22/s at 13:38 and 1.18/s at 13:39 to 0.87/s at 13:40 and 0.32/s at 13:41, was 0 from 13:42 through 13:49, and resumed at 0.71/s at 13:50 and 1.22/s at 13:52; getAdsByCategory and getRandomAds follow the same gap. ad recorded no ERROR-status spans in that period (all ad error-operation rates 0).

Deployment ad was rolled out at 13:39:10-13:39:13Z: event ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set ad-d89765fb5 from 0 to 1' and ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate for pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz (13:39:10), pod Scheduled 13:39:10, container Created 13:39:11 and Started 13:39:12, then 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0' (13:39:13) with pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq 'Killing: Stopping container ad' and SuccessfulDelete (13:39:13). These 9 ad events are the only Kubernetes events in otel-demo in the whole authorized window.

The replacement ad pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz reports phase Running, condition Ready=True with lastTransitionTime 13:39:13Z (one second after container start 13:39:12Z), container ready=true, started=true, restartCount 0, and no previous container instance exists.

Neither the old ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 nor the new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 defines a readinessProbe or livenessProbe; both use image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, containerPort 8080, the same env (AD_PORT=8080, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, OTLP endpoint to otel-collector) and the same resources (limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi, requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi).

Deployment ad has replicas 1 with strategy RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, and its pod template has no readiness probe, so the replacement pod counted as available immediately when its container started; the Service ad selects opentelemetry.io/name=ad on port 8080 and its Endpoints currently resolve to the new pod IP 100.96.1.122 on node i-00afa9d1463304f93.

The only log line retained for the new ad container is 'Ad service starting.' at 2026-11-16T13:43:23.903Z, i.e. about 4 minutes 11 seconds after the container's startedAt 13:39:12Z; there is no previous ad container instance and no further ad log lines in the window.

frontend-proxy shows its own error spans in the same interval: at 13:45Z 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 1.052/s and 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR 1.048/s against non-error rates of 11.90/s and 11.91/s, and its error rate follows frontend's curve (0.0048/s at 13:17, 0.237/s at 13:40, peak 2.10/s at 13:45, back to 0 at 13:52).

Current cluster state: all 21 otel-demo pods are Running (ad pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz created 13:39:10Z, container started 13:39:12Z, restartCount 0) and all 21 otel-demo deployments report ready/available replicas equal to desired (1/1).

Causal chain: the ad rollout replaced the only serving ad pod with a pod that Kubernetes marked Ready at 13:39:13Z because no readinessProbe exists, while the AdService process was still starting (log at 13:43:23Z, first served GetAds spans around 13:49-13:50). During that window the ad Service endpoint (100.96.1.122) led frontend's gRPC GetAds calls to fail (STATUS_CODE_ERROR client spans plus tcp.connect errors), which made /api/data and page requests return errors and pushed frontend's RequestErrorRate above 0 from 13:40:21Z until roughly 13:51.

The AdService process's slow start (container started 13:39:12Z, 'Ad service starting.' 13:43:23Z, first served spans about 13:49-13:50) may be aggravated by the pod's low CPU limit of 50m (requests 10m) combined with Java/flagd initialization; this is not proven by the evidence available and no CPU throttling metric was observed.

The replacement ad pod was not damaged: it is Running, Ready and has restartCount 0, the old pod's termination was the controller's scale-down ('Killing: Stopping container ad', ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete, Deployment ScalingReplicaSet), not Evicted or OOMKilled, and ad itself emitted no ERROR-status spans during the gap; the failure was a serving/availability gap rather than an application error burst or a crashloop.

Rejected: a node-level fault on i-00afa9d1463304f93, where the ad pod runs. In the same 13:45Z snapshot the other services on that node (accounting, currency, kafka, product-catalog, shipping) show 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate, and no node-related event appears in the window.

Rejected as the primary cause: a failure of frontend's other dependencies. frontend's cart, checkout, product-catalog and recommendation client spans show 0 error rate throughout 13:36-13:56, and those services emit no error spans in the period, so the errors are confined to the AdService path.

Add a readinessProbe (gRPC or TCP on port 8080) to the ad Deployment (and any other otel-demo workloads without one) so a rolling update keeps the old pod serving until the new AdService process actually accepts connections; consider maxUnavailable 0 for single-replica deployments.

Measure and, if confirmed, raise the ad container's CPU limit (currently 50m with a 10m request) so JVM/flagd startup completes in seconds rather than minutes, and use a startupProbe to bound slow starts without flapping.

gaps: No Prometheus rules were returned (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with no filter both returned no_data), so the alert's exact expression/threshold could not be verified; the alert annotation's 2.3556 value could not be matched to a specific series.

kube-state-metrics series were absent in this Prometheus for the queried windows: kube_pod_owner/kube_replicaset_owner (get_series), kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{deployment="ad"} and kube_pod_container_info (all no_data), so per-minute deployment availability and image digests around 13:39Z could not be checked.

Jaeger returned no frontend traces after about 2026-11-16T13:36:55Z (traces_search for 13:45-13:47 was no_data), so the exact gRPC status/detail text on the failing GetAds spans during 13:40-13:49 is unknown; the error observations come from trace-derived metrics (status_code label) only.

The old ad pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq was deleted, and the new pod has no previous container instance, so its termination reason/exit code and its own logs at the moment of the scale-down are unavailable.
The frontend container produced no log lines in the 13:38-13:56 window (fetch_pod_logs returned 0 lines), so frontend-side application error text could not be read.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so what changed in Deployment ad at 13:39:10Z (which Helm/config change produced the new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5, whose visible pod template fields are identical to the old ReplicaSet) could not be established.
No Kubernetes events outside the nine ad events were retained in the namespace for the authorized window, so any cluster-level cause of the rollout is unknown.
next_steps: Check the deployment/Helm change history and audit log for otel-demo/ad around 2026-11-16T13:39:10Z to identify what triggered the ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5.
Verify on the ad pod whether the AdService JVM startup is CPU-throttled (container CPU limit 50m) and how long it takes to listen on port 8080.
Confirm the alerting rule expression for RequestErrorRate in the Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration, since it is not loaded in the queried Prometheus.
Add a readinessProbe / startupProbe to the ad Deployment and re-test a rolling update to confirm zero-downtime behavior.
